summary: Ports the EQL release pipeline (npm package, eql-bindings crate, SQL bundle, docs bundle, postgres-eql image) from the dead packages/eql/.github/ deposit to root workflows, kept inert by a switch derived from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS in scripts/release-gate.mjs. The only change that is live on merge for already-shipping packages is to the shared release.yml: a new workflow_dispatch trigger and a new `classify` job that every JS/FFI publishing job now depends on and is gated on (`mode == 'production'`). The root rebuild-docs.yml (docs webhook on @cipherstash/stack tags) is also removed. Every EQL publishing path is latent until the cutover deletes the FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entry, and the material risks sit there: an npm release can complete while the SQL/docs/image chain does not, with no automatic re-drive; the SQL attached to the GitHub release and baked into the image is rebuilt from source under `rust = latest` rather than taken from the bytes that shipped on npm; release-plz publishes the crate on its own trigger, independent of the release gate; and the production npm half of the switch is held by a different reader (the gate) than the other four artefacts. CI on the head commit is all green, including the job that runs the script self-tests that pin these gates, but none of the armed paths has ever executed. Impact is medium; verdict focused_review_required, with the latent scenarios best addressed before the cutover rather than before this merge.

behaviour_changes.description: release.yml gains a `workflow_dispatch` trigger and a `classify` job. `ffi-artifacts`, `publish-ffi` and `release` (the live JS and FFI npm publishing jobs) now need `classify` and run only when it reports `production` (push to main, or dispatch against main). A dispatch against main behaves like a push to main.

New EQL production chain in release.yml: after `release` (changesets publish) reports that @cipherstash/eql was published, `eql-sql` builds and creates the eql-<V> GitHub release, `eql-docs` attaches docs, `eql-image` dispatches release-postgres-eql-image.yml. New prerelease chain dispatched from a non-main branch whose HEAD subject starts `chore(release):` builds SQL/docs, publishes the npm prerelease via OIDC, tags, and dispatches release-plz. All are gated on `eql-armed`.

Inertness is derived: scripts/eql-pipeline-armed.mjs reports armed=true when @cipherstash/eql is absent from FROZEN_PUBLISHERS. The production npm publish of @cipherstash/eql is not behind this switch; it is held by release-gate.mjs failing the `gate` job.

New root release-plz.yml publishes the eql-bindings crate (crates.io OIDC, contents: write, GPG key) on any push to main touching packages/eql/** or on dispatch, gated only on `eql-armed`, not on the release gate or on the npm publish having happened.

New root release-postgres-eql-image.yml (dispatch only, gated on eql-armed) builds SQL from source and pushes ghcr.io/cipherstash/postgres-eql for PG14-17; Dockerfile source label now points at cipherstash/stack.

The @cipherstash/eql prepublishOnly verifier now requires the bundled SQL to carry `COMMENT ON SCHEMA eql_v3 IS '<package version>'` (was a substring check for `eql_v3` that always passed); npm-publish.mjs sends prereleases to their channel dist-tag instead of `latest` (PRE_GA_LATEST false).
The root rebuild-docs.yml, which POSTed to DOCS_WEBHOOK_URL on `@cipherstash/stack@*` tag pushes, is deleted; a test asserts no root workflow references DOCS_WEBHOOK_URL.

Lint/guard scope widened: lint-no-workflow-caching covers the four new EQL workflows and audits Docker/release-plz/GPG actions; lint-release.yml actionlints them and shellchecks prepare-bindings-assets; lint-no-eql-registry-pins skips `.claude`; root `pnpm dev` filter changed to './packages/**'.

failure_scenarios.title: After cutover, npm publishes EQL V but the SQL/docs/image chain does not, and a re-run cannot re-drive it
failure_scenarios.trigger: Pipeline armed; on the push that publishes @cipherstash/eql@V, `eql-sql` (or `eql-docs`) fails — e.g. a build failure, the GHCR/release permission not yet in place, or a runner fault — after `release` has already published to npm.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The EQL production chain keys on `release.outputs.eql_published`, which is computed from changesets' `publishedPackages` in that run (release.yml:508-532). The npm publish happens first and is irreversible. A fresh run (or 'Re-run all jobs') re-runs `changeset publish`, finds V already on npm, emits nothing, and the comment at release.yml:504-507 treats that skip as correct. Only 'Re-run failed jobs' preserves the earlier outputs; there is no workflow_dispatch path to rebuild a production SQL/docs release for an existing version (dispatch against main reclassifies as production and hits the same empty output).
failure_scenarios.consequence: @cipherstash/eql@V (and, independently, the crate) exist with no eql-V GitHub release, docs bundle or image; consumers fetching the SQL bundle by release tag get a 404 until someone hand-builds it. Recoverable manually, but the five-artefact lockstep the PR describes is broken for that version.

existing_verification.description: eql-pipeline-armed.test.mjs asserts which jobs carry the eql-armed guard; it does not model a partial-failure re-run.

missing_verification: No test or documented runbook for re-driving eql-sql/eql-docs/eql-image for a version already on npm.
The production EQL chain has never executed in this repository.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add a dispatch input (or separate workflow) that rebuilds and attaches the SQL/docs release for an explicit, already-published version; document 'Re-run failed jobs only' in the cutover runbook.

failure_scenarios.title: SQL attached to the GitHub release and baked into the image is rebuilt, not the bytes npm and the crate shipped
failure_scenarios.trigger: Pipeline armed; the Rust toolchain resolved by `rust = latest` (or any other build input) differs between the commit that produced the committed SQL and the release run.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: npm and the crate ship the committed, stamped SQL (verify-release-assets.mjs and the release-plz preflight check the stamp). `eql-sql` instead runs `mise run --force build --version V` from source (_build-eql-sql.yml:87), and the image workflow builds again (release-postgres-eql-image.yml:97-100). The mise config pins rust to `latest` (packages/eql/mise.toml:11) and AGENTS.md itself states nothing proves regenerating from source reproduces npm's published bytes. The stamp will agree, so the stamp-based checks cannot detect a byte difference.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Three different SQL payloads can carry the same version: the GitHub release asset's digest disagrees with the npm package's release-manifest, and a database installed from the image or the release asset can carry functions that differ from what `stash eql install` installs at the same version. Silent; no check compares them.
missing_verification: No step compares the rebuilt release SQL (or image SQL) digest with the release-manifest.json committed for V.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Attach the committed, already-verified SQL from packages/eql/packages/eql/sql (or packages/eql/crates/eql-bindings/sql) instead of rebuilding, or fail the job when the rebuilt digest differs from the committed manifest.

failure_scenarios.title: release-plz publishes the crate on a push the release gate refused
failure_scenarios.trigger: Pipeline armed; a push to main touching packages/eql/** carries a crate version not yet on crates.io while release.yml's `gate` fails or `changeset publish` fails (any other package problem, frozen-bytes skew, npm outage).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: release-plz.yml runs on its own `push` trigger and its `release` job is gated only on `eql-armed` (release-plz.yml:26-44, 75-78). eql-pipeline-armed.mjs deliberately does not consult the registry or the gate. Nothing ties the crate publish to the npm publish succeeding in the same commit.
failure_scenarios.consequence: eql-bindings@V is on crates.io (irreversible; can only be yanked) while @cipherstash/eql@V and the SQL release are not, breaking the one-version-five-artefacts invariant until a later release catches up.

existing_verification.description: The release-plz preflight verifies the committed SQL stamp and manifest match the crate version before publishing.

missing_verification: No check that the npm package at the same version is published (or will be) before the crate goes out.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Have release-plz.yml check that @cipherstash/eql@<crate version> is on npm before publishing (or dispatch it from release.yml after `release` reports eql_published, as the prerelease path already does).

failure_scenarios.title: Production npm half of the EQL switch is held by a different reader than the other four artefacts
failure_scenarios.trigger: Someone relaxes or breaks release-gate.mjs's frozen-publisher refusal while the FROZEN_PUBLISHERS entry remains (or the gate's checks pass because the committed version already exists on npm and a new version is introduced by a path the gate does not see).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: The production `release` job runs `changeset publish` gated on `needs.gate.result == 'success'` only (release.yml:356-363); @cipherstash/eql is not in changesets' ignore list per AGENTS.md. eql-armed gates the other jobs. AGENTS.md:335-356 states nothing asserts the two readers agree.
failure_scenarios.consequence: @cipherstash/eql could be published to npm from this repository (or attempted and fail mid-publish) while eql-armed reports false and the SQL/docs/crate/image all skip — the outcome the derived switch exists to prevent.

existing_verification.description: release-gate.mjs runs in CI at PR time ('Lint — this tree can be published' step in the Run Tests job), which passed on the head commit.

missing_verification: No test asserting the gate refuses to publish @cipherstash/eql whenever eqlPipelineArmed() is false.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Add a test (or a guard in the release job) that ties the production EQL npm publish to eql-armed, e.g. fail `release` if publishedPackages contains @cipherstash/eql and armed != 'true'.

failure_scenarios.title: Live JS/FFI releases now depend on the new `classify` job
failure_scenarios.trigger: Any push to main (live immediately on merge); `classify` fails or does not output `production` (checkout failure, runner fault, or a later edit to its shell).
failure_scenarios.mechanism: `ffi-artifacts`, `publish-ffi` and `release` now need `classify` and require `mode == 'production'` (release.yml:194-207, 356-358). `release` uses always(), so a failed classify yields an empty mode and the release is skipped rather than failed.
failure_scenarios.consequence: A release that should have published @cipherstash/stack/FFI packages is skipped; the run may not be red for `release`. Recoverable by re-running.

existing_verification.description: workflow-dispatch-job-conditions.test.mjs models a dispatch against main classified as production and requires every non-prerelease job to run; script tests ran in the Run Tests jobs, which passed. actionlint check passed.

missing_verification: The first push to main after merge is the first real execution of `classify` on the live release path.
failure_scenarios.mitigation: Watch the first post-merge release run; consider making `classify` failure fail the run visibly (the eql-summary job covers EQL only).

verification_gaps.description: None of the armed EQL paths (production chain, prerelease chain, release-plz release, image push) has executed in this repository; tests are static assertions over workflow YAML and job conditions.
No digest comparison between rebuilt SQL (GitHub release, image) and the committed release manifest that npm/crate ship.
No assertion that the gate and eql-armed agree about @cipherstash/eql, and no ordering between the crate and npm publishes.

recommended_controls.description: Review release.yml `classify` and the `needs`/`if` changes on `ffi-artifacts`, `publish-ffi` and `release`; these are the only parts live on merge for already-shipping packages. Watch the first post-merge release run.
Before the cutover, make eql-sql (and the image) use or verify against the committed, stamped SQL so the GitHub release and image bytes match what npm and the crate ship.
Add a test that the production npm publish of @cipherstash/eql is refused whenever eqlPipelineArmed() is false, and a check in release-plz.yml that npm already has the crate's version.
Add a re-drive path (dispatch with explicit version) for the EQL SQL/docs/image release of an already-published npm version, and document it in the cutover runbook.
At cutover, cut a prerelease first through the dispatch path to exercise SQL, docs, npm, crate dispatch end-to-end before the first production final.

release job needs classify and is gated on always() && mode == 'production' && gate success; no eql-armed condition.
